Base rate: the last ten waves run 33–39, mean ≈35.7, with recent waves clustering 33–36 (last: 35). Week-to-week changes are large for a ~1,600n poll (+4,−3,+2,−1,+3,−5,+2,−3,+2), abs mean ≈2.8, consistent with sampling noise of ~1.7–2.0 pts plus a mildly declining trend. Naive extrapolation of the last 4-wave average (33–36) gives ~34.5.

Inside view: coverage points to record lows in net approval (−27 to −29 mid-August, then a slight rebound to −26 with 35% approve in the Aug 18 wave). Drivers — renewed Iran strikes/Strait of Hormuz, economic discontent, GOP softening (Republican approval down to ~69–76%) — are structurally negative, worth maybe −0.3 to −0.5 vs. flat. Mean reversion after a small uptick argues for a touch lower (−0.3). No obvious rally event before Aug 21–24 fielding. Net: ~34.4.

Pre-mortem: most likely failure is treating noise as trend — this series has bounced 39 and 33 within three weeks, so a print of 32 or 38 is quite possible; also possible a genuine floor exists near 33 (hardened partisan base ~33–34) so further downside is limited, or a modest bounce as with the −26 reading. Correction: keep the mean near the recent center rather than extrapolating decline, and widen the sd.

Calibration: with observed inter-wave swings of 2–5 points, one-sd ≈2 points is appropriate (true value inside 32.4–36.4 about two-thirds of the time).

{"mean": 34.5, "sd": 2.0}
